eplaces the client's required and optional saved-server attachments without round-tripping the whole config. Composed server-side
from the client's current config, so every other setting is preserved, and `expectedConfigId` is required so two concurrent server
replacements cannot silently lose one.\n- [Duplicate a client](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/clients/duplicate-a-client.m
d): Creates a new client carrying the selected client's current config, and responds `201` with the copy's detail. Purely additive
: the source is untouched.\n- [Validate a server](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-diagnostics/validate-a-server.md):
Connects to the server, initializes the MCP session, and returns a connection snapshot (server info, negotiated capabilities). The
same check the hosted inspector runs when you connect a server.\n- [Run the doctor](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-
diagnostics/run-the-doctor.md): Runs the full doctor workflow (probe → connect → initialize → capabilities → primitives) and retur
ns a step-by-step report. The richest signal for \"is this server healthy, and why not.\"\n- [Check OAuth requirement](https://doc
s.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-diagnostics/check-oauth-requirement.md): Lightweight, no MCP connection: reports whether the ser
ver is configured to require an OAuth grant.\n- [List tools](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-tools.md): Retu
rns the server's tools as a collection page. Each item is the MCP tool definition (`name`, `description`, `inputSchema`, ...).\n-
[List prompts](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-prompts.md): Returns the server's prompts as a collection pag
e.\n- [List resources](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-resources.md): Returns the server's resources as a co
llection page.\n- [Read a resource](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/read-a-resource.md): Reads a single resource
by URI and returns its contents.\n- [List server skills](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-server-skills.md):
Returns the Agent Skills a connected server serves over the MCP skills extension (SEP-2640), including skills it advertises that M
CPJam declines to load. Not paginated: the catalog is drained server-side, because duplicate detection spans the whole listing.\n-
[Get a server skill](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/get-a-server-skill.md): Fetches one skill by URI and verifi
es it before returning a byte: the SKILL.md digest against the manifest, the fetched frontmatter against what the listing advertis
ed, and the name against the URI. Reaches skills a partial listing never mentioned. When a check fails the response carries a `ref
usal`…\n- [Read a server skill's supporting file](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/read-a-server-skills-supporting
-file.md): Reads one supporting file belonging to a skill, checking its byte length and digest against the skill's own manifest. T
he manifest is the read allowlist and is re-fetched here rather than accepted from the caller, so a request cannot authorize its o
wn read.\n- [Export a server snapshot](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/export/export-a-server-snapshot.md): Lists tools, res
ources, and prompts in one call and returns a single JSON snapshot: handy for diffing a server's surface over time in CI.\n- [Call
a tool](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/call-a-tool.md): Executes a tool on the server and returns the MCP `CallT
oolResult` plus an additive `durationMs` (wall-clock time of `executeTool`). Tool-level failures (`isError: true` in the result) a
re **successful calls**: the server answered; only transport/auth errors use the error envelope.\n- [Render a prompt](https://docs
.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/render-a-prompt.md): Renders a prompt with arguments and returns the MCP `GetPromptResult` dir
ectly (`description?`, `messages`).\n- [Render an MCP App widget headlessly](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/rende
r-an-mcp-app-widget-headlessly.md): Call an MCP App tool and mount its `ui://` widget in real headless Chromium running the produc
tion host bridge, then report whether it rendered, what it logged, what it was blocked from fetching, and the widget as an accessi
bility tree with addressable elements.\n- [Create a retained widget session](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/creat
e-a-retained-widget-session.md): Available only on the local Inspector that created the session; hosted deployments return 404. Re
quires a verified user or API key. A session is bound to the original subject, project and server and expires after its idle timeo
ut. Executes the tool and retains its App in one local Chromium context.…\n- [Read a retained widget snapshot](https://docs.mcpjam
.com/api-reference/execution/read-a-retained-widget-snapshot.md): Available only on the local Inspector that created the session;
hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verified user or API key. A session is bound to the original subject, project and server
and expires after its idle timeout. Returns an accessibility tree and addressable elements without replay…\n- [Act on a retained
widget](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/act-on-a-retained-widget.md): Available only on the local Inspector that c
reated the session; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verified user or API key. A session is bound to the original subject
, project and server and expires after its idle timeout. Runs one coordinate action with fresh project/server authorization.\n- [R
un a retained widget step](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/run-a-retained-widget-step.md): Available only on the l
ocal Inspector that created the session; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verified user or API key. A session is bound to
the original subject, project and server and expires after its idle timeout. Runs one semantic action or assertion, using the sam
e locator vocabul…\n- [Close a retained widget session](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/close-a-retained-widget-se
ssion.md): Available only on the local Inspector that created the session; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verified user
or API key. A session is bound to the original subject, project and server and expires after its idle timeout. Disposes the origi
nal owner's browser. Returns closed=false if no mat…\n- [List a suite's settings history](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/ev
al-suites/list-a-suites-settings-history.md): One entry per committed edit to the suite's settings, newest first: who made it, whi
ch STORED fields moved, the note they left, how many runs were launched against it, and the revision group that ties one request's
writes together. Rows carry no configuration snapshots. Send a `revisionNumber` back…\n- [Attach one environment to a suite (atom
ic append)](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-suites/attach-one-environment-to-a-suite-atomic-append.md): APPEND one proj
ect environment to the suite's attachments, if it is not already there.\n- [List a server's accounts](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-
reference/server-accounts/list-a-servers-accounts.md): The accounts this server signs in with that you can see: your own personal
accounts, or, on a server shared with the project, its project accounts. Another member's personal account never appears. METADATA
ONLY: no account response carries a token.\n- [Get a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/get-a-
server-account.md): One account, by id or name. Another member's personal account answers `404`, the same as a missing one. A name
two accounts share answers `409` with `details.code: \"account_name_ambiguous\"` and both ids in `details.accountIds`.\n- [Upload
tokens to a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/upload-tokens-to-a-server-account.md): Creates
the account (`201`) or replaces its token in place (`200`, same id). A well-formed account id never creates one: an unknown id is
`404`. Any other reference is a name, and a name no account has creates the account.\n- [Delete a server account](https://docs.mcp
jam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/delete-a-server-account.md): Deletes the account and its stored token. The token's issuer is
asked to revoke it where the issuer supports revocation (best effort), which also invalidates any copy of the same token you hold
